Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:

- Credit supply and demand: SLOOS shows banks eased standards for C&I and CRE and reported stronger C&I demand across large, middle-market, and small firms, with increased credit line inquiries. Easing was driven by improved economic outlook, competition, higher risk tolerance, and solid liquidity/capital positions. This reinforces the FOMC’s view of robust activity and argues for imminent liftoff and ending net purchases as signaled.

- Household sensitivity: While banks eased standards across many consumer categories, SLOOS indicates weaker demand for residential real estate loans (including GSE and subprime) and that banks expect deterioration in household credit performance (credit cards, autos, nonconforming jumbo) as rates rise. That argues for a well-telegraphed, orderly normalization to avoid an abrupt tightening in household credit.

- Market and global nuance: Foreign banks reported roughly unchanged C&I demand, a mild offset to strong domestic business demand. Continued use of floor-system tools (IORB, ON RRP, repo ops) and reinvestments aligns with maintaining smooth market functioning as policy tightens.

Net: Relative to the FSR-only read, SLOOS tilts the stance slightly more hawkish given strong business credit conditions and easing standards, though household headwinds temper the pace.
